trial_court: Family Court, Bombay, M. J. Petition No. 1036 of 1989
case_name: Sunil Hansraj Gupta vs Payal Sunil Gupta
facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for judicial separation and custody of the two minor children. The wife took out a notice of motion for interim reliefs, including maintenance. The trial court granted maintenance to the wife and children.

legal_principles.principle: An appeal shall lie from every judgment or order, not being an interlocutory order, of a Family Court to the High Court both on facts and law.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), or in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or in any other law, an appeal shall lie from every judgment or order, not being an interlocutory order, of a Family Court to the High Court both on facts and law.

legal_principles.principle: A judgment of a Family Court shall contain a concise statement of the case, the point for consideration, the decision thereon and the reasons for such decision.
legal_principles.held: Section 17 reads thus: 'Judgment of a Family Court shall contain a concise statement of the case, the point for consideration, the decision thereon and the reasons for such decision.'

outcome.final_order: The husband was directed to pay Rs. 10,000/- per month towards maintenance to the wife and Rs. 5,000/- to each of the two minor children.
